title: Taking notes with different writing devices influences learning processes but not performance: an EEG study comparing ink pens, digital pens, and keyboards
independence: primary experiment; no claim of independence from all literature
limits: short pseudoword lectures; immediate tests only; no raw EEG reanalysis from public paper; small Korean undergraduate sample

title: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Keyboard: Advantages of Longhand Over Laptop Note Taking
independence: primary experiment; source of the original mechanism claim
limits: older student samples; lecture and quiz tasks; Study 3 explicitly includes review interaction; not a universal device trial

title: Taking Notes on a Laptop versus by Hand: Effects on Immediate Learning
independence: primary replication; overlaps topic and lectures with S2, and mini-meta includes related primary studies
limits: immediate or short-delay testing; equivalence bound excludes only large effects; does not test sustained revision or accessibility

title: Typed Versus Handwritten Lecture Notes and College Student Achievement: A Meta-Analysis
independence: synthesis; overlaps many primary studies with S2/S3 and other reviews
limits: study-level moderators are not randomized; only 7 of 49 effects unpublished; incomplete reporting of lecture and learner characteristics; no disability-specific synthesis

title: Effect of Typing Ability on Learning Gain in Typing Note-taking
independence: separate report; quantitative independence cannot be audited from exposed text
limits: no accessible sample size, effect size, timing, covariate, or missing-data details; use as hypothesis only

title: Typed Versus Handwritten Note-Taking: A Meta-Analysis of Learning Outcomes
role: independent dissertation synthesis and moderator framework
independence: synthesis; overlaps primary literature with S2/S3/S4; not an independent participant sample
limits: dissertation evidence base; study-level confounding of modality, style, review, intention, and speed remains; no disability meta-analysis

title: R1 round 002 report
role: candidate claims and search lead only
independence: not independent evidence; claims are audited against S1-S6
limits: identity frozen as UNVERIFIED_RAPID_EVIDENCE_SCANS; cannot be promoted without this R2 audit
